changed_categories: per-lab -files.json and matching in-package FILES.json mirror
scope.allowlist_mirror_reason: Existing packaging contract requires parent -files.json and packaged FILES.json to be identical; both now include the regression file.

policy.mode: reject implicit PG* defaults at startup/SQL entry; clean all child environments
policy.pg_bin: Select tool directory before scrubbing child environment; existing state retains its saved binary directory.
policy.pghost: Accepted but overridden by explicit owned Unix-socket host in every DSN; /nonexistent compatibility tested.
policy.database_url: Ignored in Python; removed from child environments.
policy.rejected_names: Every other environment name beginning PG, including empty and unknown names. This deliberately includes PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPORT even though their values are overridden.
policy.error_disclosure: Variable names only, sorted; synthetic password/service/passfile values verified absent from CLI errors.
policy.passfile: Every admin/student DSN supplies an owned-root empty.pgpass, regular file, same OS UID, mode 0600, length zero; nofollow/nonblocking open; symlink/nonempty/mode/nonregular cases refused.
policy.cleanup: status uses clean pg_ctl. stop checks marker/PID, then performs server identity verification through a clean Python dsn child, then fast-stops only the saved explicit data directory.
policy.threading: Does not mutate process-global os.environ during connections; D03 threaded business regressions passed.

implementation_differences: Added check_environment before start/connect/verify_server/raw_dsn and all non-cleanup CLI commands.
Added child_environment and supplied env explicitly to run and interactive psql subprocess.
Added private empty_passfile validation/creation and explicit passfile on every DSN.
Changed stop identity verification from in-process connect to clean sys.executable labctl.py dsn child; failed identity check still prevents stop.
Added 50 identical environment test cases per lab without changing existing conftest/business tests.
Updated three-language README environment policy, scope limits, fixture explanation, and exact new test totals.
Added tests/test_environment.py to both layers of allowlists.

runtime.python: CPython 3.13.15 (uv run python --version in each clean copy)
runtime.postgres: 18.6 Homebrew; lab VERSION_NUM=180006 verified by live identity checks

negative_mocks_per_lab.24_variable_cases: psycopg.connect, subprocess.run and load_state all asserted not called; errors contain exact name only.
negative_mocks_per_lab.8_entrypoint_cases: start/reset/raw_dsn/verify_server and CLI start/dsn/reset/psql reject before state/SQL/process work.
negative_mocks_per_lab.empty_unknown_and_secret_values: empty PGSERVICE and synthetic unknown PG_FUTURE_DEFAULT refused; sorted name-only diagnostics checked.
negative_mocks_per_lab.identity_failure: mocked clean identity child fails; no pg_ctl stop command issued.

controlled_pollution_evidence.direct_cli_additional_values: Synthetic invalid PG_BIN and ignored PGHOST; saved binary path remains usable for stop/status.
controlled_pollution_evidence.targets: Only newly created owned private-socket clusters and loopback listeners bound by the tests themselves; synthetic service/passfiles, no real user credentials.
controlled_pollution_evidence.home_passfile_evidence: Real private connection under synthetic HOME/.pgpass canary yields conn.pgconn.password == b""; psql succeeds using explicit private passfile; canary file unchanged.
controlled_pollution_evidence.cleanup_evidence: Under simultaneous pollution: running status succeeds, stop succeeds, stopped status=3, repeated stop succeeds, restart refuses; clean restart restores identical saved state.
controlled_pollution_evidence.no_leak_observed: CLI outputs contain rejected names but not synthetic password, service name or service/passfile path values. Loopback fixtures observed no queued connections.
controlled_pollution_evidence.proof_limit: Only the enumerated regression assertions and live paths were tested. No claim that all attacks, credential channels, or same-user/root tampering have been proven safe.
